## 1. ALPHA-01's remaining funded refusal: root cause and fix

**Category: a model gap, not an arithmetic bug.**
- Sizing, rounding, fees and reconciliation are all correct.
- The refusal was the correct outcome *under the old rule*.
- The rule itself was wrong: a size-reducible order was refused outright.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Timestamp | 2026-11-09 11:17 UTC (1m candle) |
| Signal id | `ENG-ALPHA-01-SOLUSD-1-16455-SELL` (bar 16455 of the run) |
| Bot · direction | ALPHA-01 · SHORT |
| Planned entry (limit 0.705) · stop | 86.14 · 86.33 |
| Fill candle | O 86.05 · H 86.78 · L 86.05 · C 86.75 |
| Ledger fill price | 86.75 (the candle close), **+0.708%** beyond the limit |
| Requested quantity | 0.08152467 SOL at $10; 8.15246631 SOL at $1,000 |
| Available · reserved | $7.07201 · $0 (at $10); $707.200874 · $0 (at $1,000) |
| Required collateral + entry fee | $7.0723 + $0.0141 (at $10) |
| Sizing decision | Capital-capped. The quantity filled the wallet at the planned price with a 0.5% price buffer plus fee |
| Ledger rejection | `INSUFFICIENT_BOT_CAPITAL` |

**Root cause:**
- The engine sizes at its planned price. The ledger fills at the live reference price.
- On this candle the market traded through the limit **and** through the stop, ending 0.71% past the limit.
- That is beyond the 0.5% sizing headroom. The ledger refused the whole order instead of filling the size the wallet could afford.

**Fix, in shared code:** the order is now reduced to fit the wallet at the fill price, never raised. It is refused only when even the reduced size is below the venue minimum.
- Worker: `worker/src/bot_ledger.ts`. The response carries `requested_qty`, `qty` and `reduced_to_fit`.
- Simulator: `engine/src/capital.mjs`.
- Engine: `runner.mjs` records the filled quantity, and the ledger check compares against it.

**Regression tests:**
- `engine/test/fleet.test.mjs`: the exact event plus a real-candle fixture. Result: no refusal at $10 or $1,000, one reduced entry, reconciles.
- `worker/test/multi_bot.test.mjs`: reduce-to-fit, plus a genuine refusal below the minimum.

**Also found:**
- That candle had already crossed the strategy's stop, so the reference strategy entered and stopped out on the same bar.
- The funded ledger fills both legs at the candle close, so it records a fee-only loss.
- This is a known limit of filling at the reference price after the candle closes. It is now recorded on the trade proof page.

**Trade-count mismatch:** the earlier doc row "122 (65/56)" was a typo for 65/57 (= 122). The funded figure "121 (65/56)" was correct and differed by exactly this refused trade. With the fix, funded ALPHA-01 has 122 trades.

## 2. BTC 1m and SOL 1m parity

**Correction:**
- The earlier statement that "some BTC profile fields are unverified" was **wrong**.
- `btcusd-1m.env` has no unconfirmed trading field. The entry and stop dropdowns are unambiguous, and the notification toggles were confirmed ON (display only).
- `solusd-1m.env`: the notification toggles and "sleep flat" were not visible in the screenshot. They have no effect on trading because sessions and sleep are off.

| Test | BTC 1m (TV: +$374.65 · PF 1.945 · DD $67.21) | SOL 1m (TV: +$382.50 · PF 2.033 · DD $61.80) |
|---|---|---|
| No warm-up (1 Nov start) | 97 trades · +$117.60 · PF 1.264 | 121 · +$325.32 · 1.782 |
| Warm-up ≥ 1 day (converged; identical trade lists up to 7 days for BTC and 21 days for SOL) | **96 · +$147.80 · 1.347 · DD $84.60** | **122 · +$356.15 · 1.856 · DD $85.46** |
| Window end extended to 12 Nov 23:00 | 102 · +$224.99 · 1.528 | 131 · +$343.24 · 1.750 |
| Window start 27 Oct … 2 Nov (any) | best +$219.13 (31 Oct) | +$335 … +$449 |
| Limit fills at the requested price when gapped | +$146.89 | +$354.95 |
| One-tick exit delay | +$147.80 | +$321.35 |
| Pivot tie rules (strict/loose combinations) | +$66.10 … +$170.73 | +$97.00 … +$356.94 |

**Conclusions:**
- Warm-up is **not** the cause: results converge after one day.
- Window boundaries, gapped-limit pricing, an exit delay and pivot tie rules do not reproduce the BTC result.
- Candles: Kraken trade-built 1m candles, UTC, matching Kraken OHLC with 0 mismatches.
  - One Kraken-wide 51-minute gap with no trades: 30 Oct 02:22 UTC, in both markets.
  - It falls before the window, inside the converged warm-up.
- Session filters are off, so chart timezone does not affect trading.

**First divergence:**
- **NOT DETERMINABLE** without TradingView's trade list. The screenshots give only summary figures.
- `engine/src/cli/compare-tv.mjs` matches trades by side and entry bar as soon as the CSV exists.

**A strong clue:**
- TradingView's BTC drawdown "$67.21 (23.55%)" implies an equity base of about $285.
- The Pine default is `initial_capital=10000`, so the owner's Properties tab differs from the script defaults.
- Commission, slippage, "on bar close" / "after order filled" recalculation, bar magnifier and margin may all differ too, and any of them changes trade outcomes.

## 6. Longer BTC 5m (the longest authentic data obtainable this session)

- **Why the window is short:** Kraken's OHLC endpoint gives only 720 candles. Longer history must be built from the public trade list, at about 10 minutes per BTC day. Data: 2026-10-20 → 11-12 23:00, with a one-day warm-up.
- **ALPHA-04 result:** 44 trades (22/22), gross +$213.37, PF 2.85, DD $23.03, net −$627.88 at 0.20%. Break-even fee 0.0507% per fill.
- **Weekly:** gross +78, −21, +64 and +93; net at 0.20% −92, −250, −231 and −55.
- **Regime coverage:** every week was a BTC decline of 2–5% (one regime), with rising volatility. Trending-up, ranging and low-volatility periods are **not covered**, so no regime conclusion is drawn.
- **Out-of-sample** (from 4 Nov): 22 trades, gross +$102.50, net −$271.65.
- **Verdict:** its gross PF is the best of the four, but it is **not profitable at 0.20%** and the sample is small.
- **Longer data needs a decision:**
  - (a) let the downloader run for hours, or
  - (b) Kraken's downloadable historical OHLCVT files. Downloading a file needs your permission.

## 7. Execution economics (verified sources; no account creation, no trading)

| Venue | Spot fee at the lowest tier (verified) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Ndax (official benchmark) | flat **0.20%** per buy/sell, "no volume tiers and no maker/taker split" ([ndax.io/fees](https://ndax.io/fees)) | Canadian; no short/margin product found |
| Kraken Pro, Canada page | Tier 1 $0+: **0.40% maker / 0.80% taker**; $2.5K+ 0.30/0.60; $10K+ 0.22/0.38; $25K+ 0.20/0.35 ([kraken.com/ca/pro/fees](https://www.kraken.com/ca/pro/fees), read 2026-11-12; page partly truncated) | Payward Canada is a restricted dealer registered with the OSC (Apr 2025, [Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/kraken-secures-restricted-dealer-registration-canada)); current status should be checked on the OSC registry. Retail entry tiers cost **more** than Ndax |
| Coinbase Advanced | Official help page returned HTTP 403; third-party figures conflict | **Not verified**; nothing concluded |

- **Maker fills are not guaranteed:**
  - A limit order is a maker fill only if it rests on the book.
  - A limit order crossed by a gap fills as taker.
  - Kraken's page does not state a rule for limit orders that execute immediately.
- **Even the best case falls short:**
  - At Kraken's $25K+ tier, a 0.20% maker / 0.35% taker round trip is 0.40–0.55%.
  - The break-even round trip is 0.0142% (SOL 5m, 150 days) to 0.099% (BTC 5m).
- **Conclusion:** no verified retail venue makes these exact strategies profitable after fees. The cost is structural, because notional per dollar of risk is huge on tight intraday stops.

## 8. RESEARCH variants (separate ids; in-sample selection, out-of-sample reporting)

**Variants tested:** higher timeframes (15m, 30m), no break-even, no trailing, neither, later break-even, and post-hoc minimum target or stop distance (approximations).

**Result: no variant is profitable out-of-sample at 0.20% on any of the four markets.**
- Variants that look better in-sample do so mostly by **trading less**: fewer trades, fewer fees.
- Out-of-sample break-even fees stay at or below about 0.05% per fill.
- BTC samples are 1–9 trades for several variants and are marked INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE.
- SOL 1m in October (in-sample) **lost money before fees** (gross −$375.73).
- Nothing here becomes a bot; the profiles are unchanged. Tables §6.

## 9. Financial reconciliation

| Scope | Identity (integer micro-USD) |
|---|---|
| Every wallet (MAIN and each bot) | available + reserved = net funding + realized (paid/received) − fees |
| Group (SOLANA, BITCOIN) | Σ of its bots' (available + reserved) = Σ their (net funding + realized − fees) |
| All wallets | Σ net funding = external deposits − withdrawals (allocations and sweeps are internal and cancel) |
| Combined book | Σ(available + reserved) = external net funding + Σ gross realized − Σ fees + Σ shortfall |
| Combined equity | book − recorded shortfall liabilities + unrealized = external funding + Σ gross − Σ fees + unrealized |

- **Correction:** the earlier backtest doc said "the sum of wallets plus MAIN equals the funding". That was **shorthand and wrong as written**. The sum equals funding **plus realized P&L minus fees**; what reconciled was the per-wallet identity above.
- **Proof:** `engine/test/fleet.test.mjs`, "financial reconciliation identities". The scenario includes a win swept to MAIN, two losses, and a short loss beyond collateral. It asserts all five identities, and that MAIN received profit while the fleet lost money.
- **Worker:** the end-to-end test asserts the per-wallet identity on D1 after every scenario, including reduce-to-fit.

## 10. Synchronization evidence

- **One bots snapshot:** `fleetStore.ts` is the only reader of `/api/dashboard/bots`. It feeds Bots, Home pipeline, Home selector, chart and Assistant.
  - Requests are deduplicated.
  - Responses are applied in request order; a test proves an older response cannot overwrite a newer one.
  - Owner actions invalidate it.
  - It refreshes on `online` and when the page becomes visible.
  - A failed refresh keeps the last snapshot with its time and an "STALE" label.
- **One funded set on Home:** `fundedTrades.ts` uses the legacy ledger plus bot-ledger rows, never twice (tested). Hero, Funded tab and Performance `?bot=` show the same net. The LOCAL TEST screenshots show −$0.59 in the hero, the tab and the bot view.
- **One status mapping:** `signalState` serves Activity, Trade Signals and notifications.
- **One identity per trade:** pending orders, fills and positions share the engine order id; the trade id is the opening order id. Bot-fill notifications link to `/bots/trade/<id>`.
- **Lifecycle events:** pending, cancelled, break-even and trailing come only from each bot's own `strategy_state` reports. They are written to `trade_events` with deterministic keys, so they appear once (end-to-end tested).
- **Charts:** current stop and target come from the shared snapshot, the same record as Bots.
- **The Assistant** reads the same snapshot.
